items.title: Dimension of a fibre over a one-dimensional local ring from the dimension at generic points
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For f: X to Y locally of finite type, a point x whose image has Noetherian local ring of dimension at most one, and an integer d such that every generic point of an irreducible component of X containing x has fibre dimension d, the lemma concludes dim_x(X_y) = d (statement lines 3596-3603). The proof replaces Y by Spec(O_{Y,y}) and X by an affine neighbourhood, reduces to X integral by handling the irreducible components separately, and then splits on whether the generic point of X maps to y (proof lines 3605-3622). In the remaining case the author factors X through Spec(B/q) for a minimal prime q distinct from the maximal ideal and applies the dimension formula: dim(O_{X,x}) + trdeg_{kappa(y)} kappa(x) <= dim(B/q) + trdeg_{kappa(q)} R(X), where dim(B/q) = 1 and the second transcendence degree equals d by the hypothesis, while dim(O_{X,x}) > dim(O_{X_y,x}) because the local ring is a Noetherian domain and the map has a kernel; the two inequalities squeeze dim_x(X_y) to d (proof lines 3623-3649). The claim is H2: the reductions are standard, while the dimension formula computation and the strict inequality between the local rings are the substantive steps.
